source_text: Iustificati itaque ex fide pacem habeamus ad Deum per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, per quem et accessum habemus in gratiam istam, in qua stamus, et gloriamur in spe gloriae Dei [n245] . Qui vobis videtis, inquit, iustificationem per peccatorum veniam fuisse collatam, firmam tenete concordiam et paribus animis Mediatoris dona laudate, cuius munere collatum nobis est, ut in hanc gratiam haberemus introitum; et eos, quos iustitia reos tenebat, quia reos nos non natura fecerat, sed voluntas, libertati reddidit et eripuit ultioni praestititque, ut, qui sperabamus aeterna supplicia, modo gloriemur in spe gloriae Dei.
pass_a_gloss: Justified therefore from faith let us have peace toward God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access into that grace in which we stand, and we glory in the hope of the glory of God. You who see, he says, that justification was conferred through a pardon of sins, hold a firm concord and with equal souls praise the gifts of the Mediator, by whose gift it has been conferred on us that we would have an entrance into this grace; and those whom justice was holding as defendants, because not nature had made us defendants but will, he rendered to liberty and snatched from vengeance and furnished that we, who were hoping for eternal punishments, now glory in the hope of the glory of God.

lemmas.lexica: LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: ‘Therefore, justified by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access to this grace in which we stand, and we glory in the hope of God’s glory’ (Romans 5:1–2). You who see that justification has been conferred on you through the forgiveness of sins, he says, hold firmly to harmony, and with united minds praise the Mediator’s gifts. By his gift we have been granted entrance into this grace. Those whom justice held guilty—because it was will, not nature, that made us guilty—he restored to freedom and snatched from retribution. He granted that we who expected eternal punishments should now glory in the hope of God’s glory.

choices.why: Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
